besu.name: Besu
besu.summary: Start with failed-frame reporting, precompile output and inclusion, and range-filter consistency. Individual replay also needs a scope decision.

erigon.name: Erigon
erigon.summary: The development build agrees on tree lookup, default filter composition, MCOPY, historical system state including trace_callMany, and the genesis reward, several of which still differ in 3.7.0. Signed-transaction validity checks and error codes need alignment with the proposal (#24329 is open), and omitted trace_filter bounds still search history instead of the proposed latest/latest default.

nethermind.name: Nethermind
nethermind.summary: 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 fixes empty trace selections, state-only output, empty-code birth/deletion markers and stack-word quantities. 2.0.0 · bec830cd still differs. Complete validation errors, tree lookup and other serialization details remain review areas.

reth.name: Reth
reth.summary: Reth 2.5.2 · df7b7fdf, the first nightly with revm-inspectors 0.44.0, fixes tree-path lookup, default filter intersection, missing-replay nulls, replay transaction hashes, the genesis reward, omitted filter bounds, the omitted trace_callMany block, new-account stateDiff markers, EIP-7702 code changes and executing initcode in vmTrace; all of these still differ in 2.6.0 · 73a3a008. Remaining work includes simulation fees, the rest of vmTrace, the SELFDESTRUCT payload (revm #3833) and error-code alignment.

build_notes.text: **The 2.5.2 build has newer source than 2.6.0.** The version number on the development branch has not received the release-only bump. Use the commit dates above and [revision comparison](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/compare/73a3a00862a8f14f89e30da8de001456f18cfae0...4630cc588430fcf3b2846e27100a5d10cff9f949).

geth.name: Geth draft fork
geth.summary: The experimental fork follows the adopted source-review stances; its checked cases agree on every assessed decision except the H12 raw-transaction block argument and simulation pending, which remain policy observations. It is not upstream Geth support or a consensus vote. Filtering remains a bounded scan; pruning still needs runtime coverage.

besu.observed: Individual transaction replay is unavailable.
besu.change: Add `trace_replayTransaction`, or agree that it is outside the supported profile.

besu.observed: A recipient-only filter returns 1 of the 2 expected calls. Every recognized `mode` value is rejected with `-32602`, including `intersection` and `union`.
besu.change: Make a one-sided query select every call matching the populated list. Accept `intersection` as the default and `union` as an explicit option; reject only unknown values.

erigon.observed: Both lists are combined with OR by default (6 records instead of 1). With `mode: "intersection"`, a one-sided filter returns `[]` instead of treating the empty side as unrestricted. The unrecognized `mode: "garbage"` is accepted and treated as union.
erigon.change: Make intersection the default. Under either mode, ignore an omitted, null or empty side. Reject unknown mode values with `-32602`.

reth.observed: 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 combines both lists with OR by default (6 records instead of 1). 2.5.2 · 4630cc58 uses intersection; one-sided and explicit-mode queries agree.
reth.change: Ship the default-intersection behavior already present in 4630cc58, retaining explicit union.

nethermind.observed: `mode: "union"` returns the intersection (1 record instead of 6) and `mode: "garbage"` is accepted: the filter type has no `mode` field, so every request is intersected.
nethermind.change: Add a validated `mode` field: accept `intersection` (the default) and `union`, and reject other values with `-32602`.

besu.observed: An empty sender list with a populated recipient list loses expected matches.
besu.change: Treat `[]` like an omitted list, then apply the populated list normally.

nethermind.change: Treat `[]` as unrestricted, just like an omitted address list.

reth.observed: Null address lists are rejected, while the revised draft treats them as unrestricted.
reth.change: Accept null like an omitted or empty list, then apply the other filter normally.

besu.observed: PoS blocks include a synthetic PoW reward record.
besu.change: Remove the placeholder reward. This also changes which records pagination counts.

nethermind.observed: PoS blocks include a synthetic PoW reward record. From source, genesis replay fails because the genesis parent lookup fails; #13783 fixes `trace_block(0)` and open #13801 fixes `trace_replayBlockTransactions(0)`.
nethermind.change: Remove the placeholder reward and exclude it from pagination. Return `[]` for the genesis block from block replay too.

reth.observed: From source: on a PoW-genesis chain, `trace_block(0)` and a filter from block 0 include a block reward for the genesis coinbase.
reth.change: Emit no records for the genesis block.

besu.observed: Unknown transactions can return [] and an unknown selected block returns null.
besu.change: Return `null` for an unknown transaction, so callers can distinguish absence from a transaction with no call records. Filter bounds beyond the head already return `-32602` as proposed.

erigon.observed: Missing-transaction lookup can return an RPC error, and a filter bound beyond the head returns [].
erigon.change: Return `null` for a missing transaction or path; reserve errors for unavailable history and invalid requests. Return `-32602` for a filter bound beyond the head or a reversed range.

nethermind.observed: Missing transactions or paths can produce exceptions/RPC errors, and a filter bound beyond the head returns -32000.
nethermind.change: Return `null` for an absent transaction or path, while preserving distinct unavailable-history errors. Return `-32602` for a filter bound beyond the head or a reversed range.

reth.observed: Missing individual replays error in 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 and return null in 2.5.2 · 4630cc58. Both return -32001 for a filter bound beyond the head. See the linked pruning cases for unavailable-history classification.
reth.change: Return `null` for absent transactions. For known transactions whose state is unavailable, use the proposed history-unavailable error (`4444`) rather than an internal error. Return `-32602` for a filter bound beyond the head (4630cc58 still returns -32001).

geth.observed: A filter bound beyond the head returns -32001.
geth.change: Return `-32602`, as the draft already does for a reversed range and as eth_getLogs does.

besu.observed: Failed frames lose result information; a failed root precompile can also lack an error.
besu.change: Keep the error on the failing frame, including a failed root precompile. Add `result: {gasUsed, output}` to REVERT frames; exceptional halts may keep omitting `result`. Use the listed labels, e.g. "Mutable Call In Static Context" and "Built-in failed", and put decoded text, not raw bytes, in `revertReason`.

nethermind.change: Add `result: {gasUsed, output}` to REVERT frames; exceptional halts may keep omitting `result`. Use the listed labels rather than "Static call violation" or "Error".

erigon.observed: A reverted CREATE reports `{address, code, gasUsed}` with the would-be address; exceptional halts use Go error text such as "out of gas: write protection", and a failed precheck is labelled "insufficient balance for transfer".
erigon.change: Report a reverted CREATE as `{gasUsed, output}` without address or code, and use the listed failure labels.

reth.observed: A reverted CREATE reports `{address, code, gasUsed}` with the would-be address; other failures fall back to Rust `Debug` names such as `NotActivated`.
reth.change: Report a reverted CREATE as `{gasUsed, output}` without address or code, and use the listed failure labels.

geth.observed: Exceptional halts use Go error text such as "out of gas: write protection" and library messages for precompile failures.

besu.observed: A successful creation reports deployed bytecode under `output`, and `creationMethod` is missing from most create frames and computed per transaction.
besu.change: Use `code` for deployed bytecode, alongside `address` and `gasUsed`. Emit `creationMethod` on every create action, from that frame’s own opcode.

besu.observed: The zero-fee call with an empty trace selection is rejected.
besu.change: Recheck after the unsigned-call fee change (H15). This case alone does not establish a separate empty-selection bug.

erigon.observed: Empty-selection requests include rejected calls; the zero-fee case also fails the fee rule.
erigon.change: Accept an empty selection and return the execution envelope. Recheck alongside H15 before treating every rejection as a separate selection bug.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd fails empty trace selections; 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 executes them.
nethermind.change: Execute the call and return its output with the unrequested components empty/null.

besu.observed: Marker probes execute wrong-chain and ordinary-code-sender transactions. Nonce, funds, intrinsic-gas and base-fee failures instead return empty success-shaped traces; these do not prove execution.
besu.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and report validation errors with the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003.

erigon.observed: Marker probes execute nonce mismatches, both insufficient-funds cases and ordinary-code-sender transactions. CREATE uses the state-nonce address. Chain, intrinsic-gas and base-fee failures are rejected with -32000. Review feedback supports stricter validation.
erigon.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and report validation errors with the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003.

nethermind.observed: Marker probes execute nonce mismatches and ordinary-code-sender transactions; CREATE uses the state-nonce address. Other invalid probes produce malformed JSON, which does not establish skipped validation.
nethermind.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and report validation errors with the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003.

reth.observed: All invalid probes in the validation corpus are rejected, using -32000 or -32003. Valid EOA/delegated controls execute, and valid execution-OOG returns a trace halt.
reth.change: Retain execution validation and report rejections with the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003.

besu.observed: Paired eth_call executes explicit zero fees with BASEFEE 0, while trace_call returns an internal error. An omitted fee is priced and charged at the base fee in trace_call but free in eth_call, and a supplied nonce that differs from the state nonce is rejected. Valid priced calls show the expected upfront debit in both methods; invalid trace fee/funding requests still produce generic internal errors.
besu.change: Match eth_call: default omitted fees to zero, zero BASEFEE for a zero effective price and ignore a supplied nonce. Retain priced accounting and return the eth_simulateV1 validation codes.

erigon.observed: eth_call uses BASEFEE 0 for explicit zero fees and debits priced gas upfront. trace_call rejects legacy zero, reprices typed zero and omitted fees to B, changes GASLIMIT and skips the sender gas debit; its stateDiff still credits tips. Both methods reject positive legacy/typed caps below B.
erigon.change: Match eth_call: default omitted fees to zero and run a zero effective price with BASEFEE zero. Preserve other block fields; enforce positive-price funding and simulate sender debit, refunds and beneficiary tips consistently.

nethermind.observed: Both tested builds use BASEFEE 0 in zero-fee eth_call but preserve B in trace_call, for explicit and omitted fees alike. Priced upfront debit matches in both methods when execution output is returned. 641592d2 fixes the release’s selection/output bugs. Fee/funding rejections are complete in eth_call but remain truncated in trace_call; see the [streaming investigation](../../docs/nethermind-streamed-errors.md).
nethermind.change: Zero BASEFEE whenever the effective price is zero, including omitted fees, and return complete validation errors with the eth_simulateV1 codes; retain normal priced accounting.

reth.observed: Both methods use BASEFEE 0 for explicit zero fees and both omit priced upfront gas payment. Both accept underpriced legacy calls and reject underpriced typed caps; a tip-only request is priced at the base fee. Method consistency agrees in 200 defined-policy pairs per build; two underfunded-value families have unclassified EVM failures. Independent priced accounting/funding checks still differ.
reth.change: Keep zero-fee compatibility. Default an omitted fee cap to zero, so a zero tip-only request runs free and a positive one is rejected as tip above cap. Reject positive legacy prices below base fee, enforce funding and simulate payment/refunds/tips during execution and later calls. Agreement with eth_call is assessed separately from this accounting requirement.

geth.observed: The captured draft eth_call uses BASEFEE 0 while trace_call preserves B for explicit zero and omitted fees: 40 defined-policy pairs differ. Priced upfront debit and positive-price rejection match across methods. The fork implements the earlier H15 proposal and is not an upstream consensus vote.
geth.change: Align the draft trace simulation with eth_call’s zero-fee BASEFEE convention for any zero effective price while retaining priced validation and accounting.

besu.observed: The `MCOPY` step omits its memory write.
besu.change: Include the bytes written at offset 32 in that step’s memory delta. Derive CALL-family `mem` from the output window rather than the caller’s final RETURN, exclude the stipend from value-CALL `cost`, include forwarded gas in precompile-call `cost`, and report a failed operation with its pre-execution cost and `ex: null`.

erigon.observed: 3.7.0 · bdc78cc4 and 3.8.0-dev · f8cfe5a7 report the `MCOPY` memory write and MLOAD memory as proposed.
erigon.change: Report a failed operation with `ex: null` and no `store`, drop the synthetic STOP at the end of code, and give SELFDESTRUCT and failed-precheck calls `sub: null`.

nethermind.observed: CALL steps have no `mem` for their output window, CREATE `cost` omits the forwarded gas, DUPn pushes n words, and `store` appears only when stateDiff is also selected.
nethermind.change: Report the CALL output window, include forwarded gas in CREATE `cost`, push n+1 words for DUPn, keep failed operations with `ex: null`, and report `store` regardless of the other selections.

geth.observed: MLOAD has no `mem` and a short CALL return reports only the returned bytes; CREATE `cost` omits forwarded gas; code that runs off its end gets a synthetic STOP; an EOA target returns a null vmTrace.
geth.change: Report MLOAD and the full CALL output window, include forwarded gas in CREATE `cost`, drop the synthetic STOP, and return `{code: "0x", ops: []}` for EOA, precompile and empty-code frames.

reth.observed: Reth 2.6.0 locks revm-inspectors 0.43.0, which reports whole-memory `mem`, pre-operation `used`, never sets `store`, and adds a synthetic STOP. The nightly takes up 0.44.0, which fixes `used` and `store`, but still reports no MLOAD memory or full CALL output window, adds the synthetic STOP and gives a failed-precheck call a `sub`.
reth.change: Report MLOAD and the full CALL output window, drop the synthetic STOP and give a call that fails its precheck `sub: null`; 2.6.0 also needs the 0.44.0 fixes for `used` and `store` (#504, #528).

besu.observed: The identity precompile returns bytes in the execution envelope but not its call frame.
besu.change: Copy the precompile’s return bytes into the call-frame result as well.

besu.observed: CREATE and SELFDESTRUCT address queries disagree with the corresponding block trace.
besu.change: Match creation by creator/created address, SELFDESTRUCT by executing account/beneficiary, and rewards by `author` on the recipient side.

nethermind.observed: From source: rewards never match `toAddress`, because the matcher reads `from`/`to` while a reward carries `author`. A failed CREATE matches its attempted address through the internal `action.To`, the same policy difference Erigon and Alloy (Reth) show through the failed result address.
nethermind.change: Match rewards by `author` on the recipient side. Give a failed CREATE no recipient match, the H23 adoption shared with Erigon and Alloy, while keeping sender-only matching and empty recipient filters unchanged.

erigon.observed: A failed CREATE matches its attempted address through the failed result address, the same policy difference Nethermind (`action.To`) and Alloy (Reth) show. From source, rewards are emitted for a coinbase in `toAddress` only in blocks the address indexes select: to-only and union filters return them, while intersection mode intersects the from and to txNum bitmaps, so `rewards-intersection` returns `[]` on both builds.
erigon.change: Give a failed CREATE no recipient match, the H23 adoption shared with Nethermind and Alloy, while keeping sender-only matching and empty recipient filters unchanged.

reth.observed: A failed CREATE matches its attempted address through Alloy’s failed result address, the same policy difference Erigon and Nethermind show. A post-Cancun SELFDESTRUCT to self has no executing account or beneficiary, so address filters miss it: revm skips the inspector callback (revm #3834).
reth.change: Give a failed CREATE no recipient match, the H23 adoption shared with Erigon and Nethermind. The SELFDESTRUCT payload follows from revm #3833 once it reaches revm-inspectors and Reth.

besu.observed: A handled child failure can mark a successful parent or sibling as failed.
besu.change: Track errors per frame; a caught failure must not change the outcome of another frame.

besu.observed: A range filter differs from concatenating the same blocks’ traces across a fork boundary.
besu.change: Trace each block from its parent’s post-block state with its own pre-block system calls, under its own fork rules, so range filtering agrees with per-block tracing. Swapping the protocol spec alone leaves rewards, withdrawals and system calls between blocks unapplied.

besu.observed: Nested precompile frames are omitted even when their value is nonzero. A CALL that fails its balance precheck has no frame, and a CREATE that fails it leaves a successful-looking frame at `[0]`, moves the real creation below it and reports the root as using no gas.
besu.change: Retain nested precompile frames with transferred or inherited nonzero value (#11360). Continue omitting zero-value nested frames and retaining root frames. Give a CALL or CREATE that fails its balance or depth precheck a failed frame with error "Insufficient balance for transfer", no result and no children, as Besu's callTracer already records it; no submitted fix covers this.

nethermind.observed: A CALL or CREATE that fails its balance precheck has no frame, and a CREATE2 address collision has no frame either. Its callTracer also omits the precheck failure.
nethermind.change: Emit a failed frame with error "Insufficient balance for transfer", no result and no subtraces for a precheck failure, and a failed create frame with error "Contract address collision" for a collision, in trace_* and in the callTracer.

geth.observed: The captured draft implementation (0a663f3c) still follows the previous rule and emits no frame for a CALL or CREATE that fails its precheck.
geth.change: Fixed on feat/trace in 07a99c67, which keeps the failed frame with the new labels; the next capture measures it.

erigon.observed: Root and nested `trace_get` requests fail or select the wrong record.
erigon.change: Interpret the selector as one `traceAddress` path: `[]` selects the root, `[0]` its first child.

nethermind.observed: `trace_get` returns a list and treats positions differently from a nested path; `[]` returns `[]`.
nethermind.change: Return one object for one `traceAddress` path. `[]` selects the root; a missing path returns `null`. This changes the response type.

reth.observed: 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 uses a flat selector; 2.5.2 · 4630cc58 selects the requested tree path and matches these cases.
reth.change: Ship the tree-path lookup already present in 4630cc58 (#27366). Existing flat-index callers need a migration path.

erigon.change: Return `trace: []` when call traces were not requested; keep the execution output independently.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd loses nonempty execution output with stateDiff-only selections; 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 retains it.
nethermind.change: Always retain output bytes. The return-42 fixture should still return its 32-byte word when only state differences are requested.

erigon.observed: Malformed raw transactions and an unknown option use error codes other than `-32602`. From source, trace_call drops `input` and every post-Berlin call field, so an `input`-only call runs with empty calldata. Open #24290 adds `input`; #24294, merged after this capture, adds `nonce`, `chainId`, `blobVersionedHashes` and `authorizationList`.
erigon.change: Use JSON-RPC invalid params (`-32602`) for malformed input, separately from execution rejection. Decode `input`, `nonce`, `chainId`, `type`, `blobVersionedHashes` and `authorizationList`, or reject them.

nethermind.observed: Malformed raw input, negative filter count and integer paths expose validation differences across the captured builds.
nethermind.change: Return invalid params (`-32602`) for malformed encoding.

besu.observed: Wrong address-list types and negative count can return results rather than invalid params.
besu.change: Validate filter types and bounds and return -32602 for invalid request shapes.

reth.observed: An integer trace_get path returns null instead of invalid params.
reth.change: Reject integer path entries with -32602; callers must convert output path integers to hex quantities.

erigon.observed: A historical beacon-root lookup includes a following block’s system update.
erigon.change: Read the selected block’s post-state, before applying the next block’s system operations. Read the first trace_callMany item at the same state as trace_call (txIndex −1). Both are fixed on main (#24056, #24293); 3.7.0 carries only the trace_call fix.

besu.observed: From source: block replay does not run the block’s pre-block system calls, so a transaction that reads the EIP-4788 or EIP-2935 contracts sees stale storage. The captured H28 probes use trace_call only.
besu.change: Apply the block’s pre-execution system calls before replaying its transactions ([Besu #10953](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/pull/10953)).

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd uses padded byte strings for VM stack words. 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 includes PR #13750 and emits minimal stack quantities; both builds still encode storage operands as a padded key and non-minimal values such as 0x00.
nethermind.change: Ship the minimal-quantity stack encoding verified in 641592d2, e.g. 0x2a rather than a 32-byte padded string, and apply it to vmTrace store keys and values.

nethermind.observed: Rejected signed transactions can leave truncated JSON on the wire.
nethermind.change: Finish validation before committing a streamed result, or ensure the error path returns one complete JSON-RPC response.

besu.observed: The initial zero-fee callMany result contains a complete JSON-RPC error envelope nested inside result.
besu.change: Return a top-level error when execution is rejected; never serialize an error envelope as a successful result.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd reports a pre-Cancun deletion as `*` to `null` for balance, nonce and code. 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 includes PR #13668 and restores the deletion markers, while retaining existing accounts after Cancun. From source, a deleted account lists its written slots as `*` to zero.
nethermind.change: Ship the account-deletion serializer fix verified in 641592d2, retain the pre/post-Cancun regression cases, and report a deleted account’s storage as `{}`.

reth.observed: Pre-Cancun account deletion loses code/nonce deletion markers. After Cancun, a SELFDESTRUCT to self reports a zero executing account and balance because revm skips the inspector callback when the opcode changes no state (revm #3834).
reth.change: Report the removed code and nonce before Cancun; preserve existing accounts after EIP-6780. Fixed by revm-inspectors #510, released in 0.44.0 and taken up by the nightly; 0.44.0 lists accessed nonzero slots as `-`, which open revm-inspectors #530 changes to `storage: {}`. The SELFDESTRUCT payload is fixed by open revm #3833, which then needs revm-inspectors and Reth uptake.

geth.observed: A deleted account lists its written slots with `-`.
geth.change: Report a deleted account’s storage as `{}`.

reth.observed: 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 omits transactionHash in individual replays; 2.5.2 · 4630cc58 includes it.
reth.change: Ship the replay metadata fix already present in 4630cc58.

reth.observed: EIP-7702 delegation code changes are missing from `stateDiff`.
reth.change: Include net authorization code set, replacement and clearing, even for existing accounts and when the subsequent execution reverts. Fixed by revm-inspectors #509, released in revm-inspectors 0.44.0 and taken up by the Reth nightly (df7b7fdf); 2.6.0 still differs until a Reth release carries it.

reth.observed: Creation `vmTrace.code` does not contain the expected executing initcode.
reth.change: Attach the creation frame’s initcode to its VM trace, including in block replay. Fixed by revm-inspectors #511, released in revm-inspectors 0.44.0 and taken up by the Reth nightly (df7b7fdf); 2.6.0 still differs until a Reth release carries it.

erigon.observed: Omitting both bounds starts at block 1 rather than head 48. Supplying only toBlock 2 searches the early range.
erigon.change: Default an omitted fromBlock to latest. Limit an entirely unbounded request to the current head; return `-32602` when an explicit end precedes that implicit start.

reth.observed: 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 starts at block 1 when both bounds are omitted, and toBlock 2 alone searches the early range. 2.5.2 · 4630cc58 defaults both bounds to latest.
reth.change: Ship the latest/latest default from 4630cc58, preserving explicit historical bounds and resource-limit errors. Return `-32602` when an explicit end precedes the implicit start.

geth.observed: The experimental draft fork follows the earlier earliest-to-latest proposal: its unbounded query starts at block 1 and its toBlock-only query searches early history.
geth.change: Align its omitted-bound behavior with latest/latest and reject the reversed range with `-32602`. This is draft-fork work, not a finding about upstream Geth trace support.

nethermind.observed: An explicit toBlock before the implicit latest start returns -32000.

besu.observed: trace_callMany with one argument returns -32602 Invalid number of params; explicit latest returns NUMBER 48.
besu.change: Accept an omitted block argument and execute against latest.

reth.observed: An omitted trace_callMany block returns NUMBER 49 on both tested builds, while explicit latest and trace_call defaults return 48. Main already defaults to latest (#27410).
reth.change: Ship the latest default from main; retain pending only when explicitly requested and supported.

besu.observed: trace_filter with safe or pending bounds returns -32603 Internal error; earliest succeeds. Pending call simulations return NUMBER 48.
besu.change: Resolve safe/finalized tags when available. Reject pending with `-32602` for filter bounds, `trace_block` and `trace_replayBlockTransactions`, rather than an internal error or latest, and accept a block hash for `trace_call` and `trace_callMany`.

reth.observed: trace_filter rejects earliest, safe and pending with -32602, although numeric bounds work. Explicit pending call simulations return NUMBER 49.
reth.change: Accept earliest, safe and finalized filter bounds, with earliest as the lowest available block. Reject pending with `-32602` for filter bounds and for `trace_block`, which currently traces a local pending block under a non-canonical hash.

erigon.observed: 3.7.0 · bdc78cc4 and 3.8.0-dev · f8cfe5a7 reject a pending filter bound with -32000 ("tracing on top of pending is not supported").

geth.observed: `earliest` resolves to block 0 rather than the lowest available block.
geth.change: Resolve `earliest` to the lowest available block, as eth_getLogs does, and keep 4444 for explicit numbers below retained history.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd omits the empty-code birth marker for transfers, empty-runtime CREATE and fresh fee recipients. 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 contains PR #13668 and fixes these cases in the fresh Fedora capture; existing-account markers remain unchanged.
nethermind.change: Ship the account-existence serialization fix verified in 641592d2. The [H17 audit](../../docs/h17-assessment-audit.md) retains the source explanation and before/after evidence.

reth.observed: A first transfer to an absent account reports balance as a change from zero and code/nonce as unchanged. revm-inspectors reserves added fields for contract creation. Simple contract-creation markers are correct, including when H15 environment bytes differ; see the [H17 audit](../../docs/h17-assessment-audit.md).
reth.change: Adopt [revm-inspectors #526](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/revm-inspectors/pull/526), released in revm-inspectors 0.44.0 and taken up by the Reth nightly (df7b7fdf); 2.6.0 still differs until a Reth release carries it. The [H17 audit](../../docs/h17-assessment-audit.md) retains the Fedora regression results.

geth.observed: Zero-to-value and value-to-zero slots on an account that exists at both endpoints are reported with `+` and `-`.
geth.change: Use `*` with 32-byte from/to words for every slot change on a surviving account; reserve `+` and `-` for account birth and deletion.

besu.observed: `trace_callMany` does not start each call at a transaction boundary, so a later call’s SSTORE uses the pre-bundle original value: the second `initial/call-many-priced` call uses 5,600 gas less than on every other build.
besu.change: Mark a transaction boundary before each call, as block replay already does, so original values, access sets, transient storage and refunds start afresh.
